orgs.name: Ezra Marfo Cancer Foundation
orgs.description: 1. Stem Cells Donor Drives and Cancer Education Workshops The Foundation organized stem cell drives and cancer education workshops in Calgary Edmonton Lethbridge the Greater Toronto Area Ottawa Winnipeg. The workshops and donor drives targeted at Canadian residents aged 17-35 as that is the eligibility age for stem cell registration. The drives were held at multicultural centers community halls churches mosques universities and college campuses. For each event a representative of the Foundation with strong stem cells and cancer knowledge as well as an external experts presented. 2. Development and distribution of Brochures on stem cells frequently asked questions To achieve the goal of advancing blood cancer and stem cells education among Canadian youth especially visible minorities the Ezra Marfo Cancer Foundation developed brochures on frequently asked stem cells questions. The brochure are in both English and French and answer questions mostly asked at stem cell donor drive events. The brochures were be vetted by Canadian Blood Services. Distribution of the brochures will commence in May of 2023. The printed brochure were disseminated at events organized by the Foundation to participants. Also brochure holders with the printed brochures will be made available at multicultural centers and at other locations frequented by people aged 17-35 years. 3. Distribution of Quarterly Newsletters The Foundation sent out electronic newsletters to those on its mailing list to further advance stem cells and blood cancer education. At every event as part of the free registration process participants were given the option to subscribe to the Foundation’s newsletter. Quarterly newsletters focusing on stem cells and blood cancers will be sent out to further help educate Canadians on stem cells and blood cancers. 4. Family Support The Foundation visited oncology units of children hospitals in Alberta to support families and also participate in some programs to benefit the families.

orgs.sub_category: Treatment / preventative care for specific disease / health condition
orgs.description: The Spina Bifida and Hydrocephalus Association of Northern Alberta (SBHANA) was founded to address the specific needs of individuals with spina bifida and hydrocephalus in Edmonton and the surrounding areas. One of our flagship programs Camp Freedom was established to provide these individuals particularly children and youth with opportunities to engage in recreational and sporting activities while fostering a sense of community and independence. Camp Freedom is a four-day overnight camp held during the summer offering a range of themed weeks tailored to the interests of our youth participants. Through a blend of recreational and sports-focused programming such as Star Performers week sledge hockey wheelchair basketball adapted soccer and adapted baseball campers have the chance to explore various activities they may not have access to elsewhere. We collaborate with community organizations and businesses to maximize these opportunities ensuring that campers can lead active and fulfilling lives. In addition to Camp Freedom SBHANA extends support to its members through various initiatives. Our Support Fund assists members in covering the costs of medical or adaptive equipment emergency expenses hospital-related out-of-town trips and other disability-related needs. We also offer funding for educational pursuits publish informative newsletters organize social events like the Christmas Party and Summer BBQ distribute educational materials host the NoLimits Support Group and provide new parent welcome bags. Our annual fundraising event has evolved into an in-person 5KM and BBQ event bringing our community together to raise funds celebrate SBHANA's accomplishments and honor our members. This event symbolizes our commitment to promoting inclusivity empowerment and a vibrant sense of belonging within the spina bifida and hydrocephalus community.

orgs.name: GLENROSE REHABILITATION HOSPITAL FOUNDATION
orgs.description: The Glenrose Rehabilitation Hospital Foundation harnesses the power of philanthropy to keep the Glenrose Rehabilitation Hospital at the forefront of innovative rehabilitative care. Donors to the Glenrose Foundation have successfully funded research medical equipment innovative programs and cutting edge technology for the Glenrose Hospital including: • The Building Trades of Alberta Courage Centre brought new robotics virtual reality a cognitive learning zone and simulation and gaming technologies to the Glenrose Hospital. The CAREN (Computer Assisted Rehabilitation Environment) is a virtual reality medical treatment system to support both military and civilian patients in healing particularly those suffering from amputations or brain injuries. PTSD research is also being conducted using the CAREN. It is the first CAREN system to be made available for patients in Western Canada. • The Reflection and Renewal Centre brings spirituality into the healthcare journey. It’s a quiet space where patients and their families can go for reflection meditation or prayer. It can accommodate people of all backgrounds and faiths and includes an ablution room meditative literature and Bluetooth speakers for music. • The Glenrose Rehabilitation Research Innovation & Technology (GRRIT) Hub which assists in developing new opportunities for meaningful improvements in the quality of life for people with physical and cognitive impairments. • The I Can Centre is a unique environment which brings adaptive technology into the lives of people with disabilities to help them achieve higher degrees of independence and allows Glenrose-quality care to expand beyond the hospital itself. • The Pediatric Family Room a suite for parents to use while their child is an in-patient at the Glenrose. • The Chadi Centre for Pediatric Rehabilitation features healing spaces for the Glenrose’s littlest patients. A pediatric gym feeding and swallowing room casting and splinting area as well as mullti-functional therapy zones ensure kids have access to the best rehabilitative care. • The Brain Computer Interface program ('BCI') which reads brain activity in pediatric patients and translates these signals into messages that external devices use to move or engage in another targeted activity. • The Omega digital scanner and carver system scans a patient's limb and then creates a negative mold for a prosthesis.

orgs.description: The organization provides support through meetings group discussions and online/social media sources to peple affected by cavernous malformation and their families and friends. The organization educates the public about cavernous malformation a rare disease as well as other medical conditions that are related such as stroke headaches migraines brain injury epilepsy etc. The organization links patients with medical professionals across Canada that are specialized in cavernous malformation. The organization provides Webinar's to those affected by cavernous malformation their friends families and caregivers with guest speakers that are considered to specialize and have expertise in the disease. The organization does outreach to similar organizations and medical professionals about cavernous malformation. The organization participates in international meetings surrounding cavernous malformation about ongoing research studies and brings this information to the patient community. We participate in brain awareness week aligned with the International Brain Research Organization. During this initiative we support our members by having meditation sessions sharing brain facts posting emulsifier free recipes hosting events by zoom for our affected members and their caregivers. During Rare Disease Day we engage in communication collaboration with other organizations share patient stories and talk about cavernous malformation as a rare disease.

orgs.legal_name: EDMONTON NEWCOMER CENTRE
orgs.description: ENC provides programs services and information to support newcomers help them find and access the resources and training needed to enhance their integration and settlement . Core pillars of our programs focus on Employment Services Settlement Services Language Services and Community Programs. ENC services provide training and education for newcomers to develop skills and find employment. We provide services for newcomers and their family in facilitating their settlement into Canada which might include social work or therapeutic services. ENC provides language training and instruction to newcomers. The Empowered Communities programs that ENC provides facilitates connections for our clients. Our Enhanced Settlement Workers in Schools program supports children and youth within the school system. Support for Kids and Youth (aka SKY Club) has activities and learning opportunities for school-age children to integrate into school culture. Civic Engagement for Newcomer Youth is a program for newcomer youth to develop as community leaders. Safe Families provides adults with skills to deal with family issues absent physical or emotional means. Wintergration offers newcomers the opportunity to enjoy Canadian winters. Our Global Garden program is a community-based project which enables food security for participants. Rainbow Refuge creates community for LGBTQ2+S newcomers. Conversation Circles and New Horizon for Seniors allows older newcomers the opportunity to network.

orgs.description: Theatre Alberta Society is a provincial arts service organization that proudly serves theatre artists enthusiasts students educators and community and professional theatre companies from across Alberta. We are dedicated to encouraging the growth of theatre in Alberta by providing the highest quality programs and services. We offer Canada's largest independent theatre library; workshops and summer schools for teens and adults urban and rural; audition employment and resource sharing services; promotional opportunities for theatre companies; and theatre news and publications. We now offer our programs and services in a variety of in-person and online formats. Theatre Alberta's core programs and services include our Library Artstrek Emerge Workshops by Request The Playbill and our website.

orgs.description: FRONTLINE TRAINING AND EDUCATION TO SHELTER AND COMMUNITY ORGANISATIONS. WE COORDINATE THE COLLECTION OF DATA FROM SHELTERS ACROSS ALBERTA TO INITIATE CONDUCT AND PARTICIPATE IN RESEARCH RELATING TO THE CAUSES IMPACTS PREVENTION AND ELIMINATION OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN CHILDREN AND SENIORS. RESEARCH INCLUDES THE DEVELOPMENT AND ANALYSIS OF SURVEYS DISTRIBUTED TO KEY POPULATIONS FOR EXAMPLE THE ALBERTA MEN'S ATTITUDES ABOUT VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN SURVEY. WE PROVIDE PUBLIC EDUCATION THROUGH OUR LEADING CHANGE CALL TO ACTION WHICH SEEKS TO EDUCATE AND INSPIRE IN COMMUNITIES SCHOOLS BUSINESSES AND INSTITUTIONS SO THAT PEOPLE LEAD FROM WHERE THEY STAND TO END DOMESTIC ABUSE. INCLUDES TRAINING YOUTH THROUGHS CHOOLS AND SPORTS TEAMS ON HEALTHY RELATIONSHIPS AND THE IMPACTS OF ABUSE TRAINING ON DOMESTIC VIOLENCE IN THE WORKPLACE AND ENGAGING WITH COMMUNITY MEMBERS INCLUDING MEN AND BOYS PROGRAMMING TO ENCOURAGE EVERYONE TO PLAY A ROLE IN ENDING DOMESTIC ABUSE. WE PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES TO SHELTER STAFF TO PARTICIPATE IN NETWORKING EVENTS AND REGULAR MEETINGS INITIATIVES SUCH AS THE DEATH REVIEW COMMITTEE AND KNOWLEDGE EXCHANGE AND SUPPORT ACHIEVE CHANGES TO POLICY AND PRACTICES TO HELP ENHANCE SAFETY FOR SURVIVORS AND ENSURE THE PROVISION OF CONSISTENT SERVICES. WE ARE FULLY COMMITTED TO HONOURING THE PRINCIPALS OF THE TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION COMMISSION TO HELP END VIOLENCE AGAINST INDIGENOUS WOMEN.

orgs.name: KIDS KOTTAGE FOUNDATION
orgs.description: THE CRISIS NURSERY PROGRAM SUPPORTS A CAREGIVER WHO IS ISOLATED LACK NATURAL SUPPORT AND STRUGGLE WITH PROBLEMS THAT REQUIRE TEMPORARY CARE FOR THEIR CHILDREN. THE CHILDREN (NEWBORN TO TEN YEARS OF AGE) ARE PROVIDED WITH TWENTY-FOUR-HOUR CARE FOR UP TO THREE DAYS BY TRAINED AND SKILLED CHILD CARE PROVIDERS AND WHILE THEY ARE IN OUR CARE WE ATTEND TO EVERY FACET OF A CHILD’S SAFETY AND WELLBEING. WE PROVIDE BOTH PHYSICAL PROTECTION AND THE EMOTIONAL SECURITY NEEDED IN WHAT IS OFTEN A STRESSFUL TIME IN THE LIVES OF THESE YOUNG CHILDREN AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. THE CRISIS NURSERY PROGRAM ALSO PROVIDES CARE FOR CHILDREN REFEREED THROUGH THE FOLLOWING WAYS; NORTHERN ALBERTA CHILDREN’S INTERVENTION SERVICES CHILDREN’S SERVICES PLACEMENT COORDINATION UNIT AND CRISIS RESPONSE TEAM FOR RECENTLY APPREHENDED CHILDREN. THESE CHILDREN MAY STAY LONGER THAN SEVENTY-TWO HOURS AS THEY AWAIT TO TRANSFER OR KINSHIP CARE PLACEMENT. FOLLOW UP PROGRAM SUPPORT IS SCHEDULED WITH THE CAREGIVERS FOR AT LEAST ONE FOLLOW-UP CONTACT AFTER DISCHARGE IN THE FAMILY’S HOME. IF NEEDED FOR FURTHER SUPPORT A FOLLOW UP WORKER WILL ENGAGE CAREGIVERS IN ADDITIONAL HOME-BASED SUPPORT TO WORK ON GOALS THAT WILL REDUCE RISK FACTOR AND IMPROVE THE FAMILIES FUNCTIONING AND WELLBEING. INVOLVEMENT THE WITH THE CAREGIVERS WILL BE COMPLETED WHEN THE SERVICE’S GOAL HAVE BEEN ACHIEVED

orgs.description: 1. To advance education by: - providing seminars workshops and presentations to the general public on topics such as exercise and nutrition eating disorders and body evaluation; - creating and distributing educational materials such as brochures and presentations for healthcare professionals educators or other specific groups on topics relating to nutrition and eating disorders; and - offering exercise classes that are trauma-sensitive based. 2. These were primarily done throughout the fiscal year through the following primary areas: - Support group programming - Trauma-sensitive exercise sessions - Awareness/dissemination of eating disorders and preventative health strategies through events or through supporting advocacy groups (i.e. Eating Disorder Awareness Week campaign a registered eating disorder awareness student group at a Canadian post-secondary institution etc)

orgs.name: Eating Disorder Support Network of Alberta Society
orgs.sub_category: Treatment / preventative care for specific disease / health condition
orgs.description: Hybrid workshops on specific topics were offered this term but all support group programming remained entirely virtual. EDSNA provided 13 multi-week support groups and 20 nights of single-session group programming during this time frame-- over 190 registrations. In addition to programming for people with eating disorders and caregivers EDSNA provided workshops on meal support body image interoception & sensory modulation and the biological underpinnings of eating disorders. Outcomes and participant feedback is monitored through anonymous self-report feedback forms; surveys consistently indicate that participants appreciate having a safe space to share ask questions and find peer support. Advertising for programming is shared on social media among other avenues all of which saw an increase in subscription. Total subscribers are as follows: Facebook (1 540); Instagram (1 847); X (formerly Twitter- 1 117); the EDSNA newsletter (1 598). Outreach and awareness initiatives during this timeframe included Eating Disorders Awareness Week (EDAW) 2024 community presentations and info booths. EDAW 2024 was marked with a social media giveaway and educational content as well as the lighting of provincial landmarks (including four new sites). Community presentations were shared with Alberta Health Services (AHS) addictions treatment teams public school division counsellors and Primary Care Networks (PCNs). Info booths were setup as part of Mental Health Week at varying educational institutions.

orgs.name: Leduc LINX Connect Centre
orgs.description: Leduc LINX Connect Centre (the 'organization') is a not-for-profit organization incorporated under the Societies Act of Alberta on December 31 2007. The organization is a registered charitable organization with the Canada Revenue Agency and as such is exempt from the payment of income tax under subsection 149(1) of the lncome Tax Act. Leduc LINX Connect Centre opened its doors on April 1 2008. This was made possible by a group of motivated persons who saw a continued need for supports for individuals with developmental disabilities in the Leduc Alberta area. A parent-driven Board of Directors was formed to carry on the task of bringing together what is now known as Leduc LINX Connect Centre (Learning Inclusion Networking X-cellence) a name chosen by the individuals supported in 2008. LINX continues to be committed to providing safe engaging services to individuals in the area as all human beings have the right to live work and play in the community of their choosing. The Day Program offers Employment Work Experience Volunteerism Community Access and a range of Classes. The Residential Program offers Support Homes Respite and Supported Independent Living (Outreach). The Youth Program offers Respite and Community Aid supports. As an organization LINX values: • The worth and dignity of human beings. • The full inclusion of all persons in the wider communities. • All persons contributing as citizens to their communities. • Working as a professional learning organization. Mission Through connections to the community LINX strives to enhance the quality of life for individuals with developmental disabilities through education employment residential and outreach services. Vision Adults and children with developmental disabilities have opportunities to experience life to their fullest potential. They experience inclusion in taking an active and valued role in society and the opportunity to reside in a community of their choosing.

orgs.name: North Saskatchewan Watershed Alliance Society
orgs.sub_category: Conservation of nature / habitat group / ecosystem preservation etc.
orgs.description: To educate and increase the public's understanding of watershed protection and its importance by developing and providing programs on the protection and improvement of water quality water quantity and the health of the North Saskatchewan Watershed. To conduct research relating to the protection of the North Saskatchewan Watershed and disseminate such research results. The NSWA is renewing its assessment of the State of the Watershed last completed in 2005 as a public education tool and a way to focus overall management of the watershed on important issues. The NSWA continues to lead collaboration at a local level with three sub-watershed alliances including education and youth-focused programming. Continued collaboration with several academic programs that are investigating different aspects of aquatic ecosystem management.

orgs.name: Elders and Angels
orgs.sub_category: Seniors’ outreach programs (housekeeping / tax preparation, etc.)
orgs.description: Last year Elders and Angels were able to achieve their goals by helping seniors with disabilities by providing them with a variety of services that could aid them in their everyday life. Through the removal of snow mowing lawns spring clean-ups fall clean-ups and housekeeping we were able to give assistance to seniors in need of our services. Elders and Angels staff and volunteers contributed over 8 000 hours in supporting our seniors to have a meaningful life. The most needed program that seniors required were programs such as house-cleaning mowing lawns and most importantly snow removal. We were able to gather a few volunteers who were willing and able to provide essential services for seniors and people with disabilities. We also took into consideration other programs that seniors suggested that would make their life much easier; therefore we have tailored our programs to meet the needs of seniors and people with disabilities living in Edmonton. We have added home care services to our specified programs such as companionship meal preparation medication reminders respite care etc. We continue to serve our seniors with humanity kindness and respect as we also prioritize privacy. Elders and Angels for some years now have become a cornerstone for many seniors. Elders and Angels will continue to support and provide unique services that will ensure social inclusion emotional well-being and productive and meaningful living for all our seniors in Edmonton! We embrace the quality of life and quality of care

orgs.name: The Altview Foundation for Gender Variant and Sexual Minorities
orgs.description: GSA Supports - Provided peer support resources and activity supports to student-led Gay Straight Alliances for 2SLGBTQ+ students and their friends/allies in schools within rural Albertan communities offered both in-person and virtually. Our supports include K-12 including elementary schools’ Rainbow Clubs. School presentations - delivering evidence-based presentations and education on a wide variety of topics including LGBTQ2S+ awareness and allyship understanding homophobia and transphobia an empathetic look at bullying and 2SLGBTQ+ history. Presentations were provided for students (class presentations) staff (professional development) and families of students (community presentations) within rural Albertan school divisions. In-person and virtual. We offer elementary schools presentations about why we choose to bully others and how to be an ally to someone in need. Safer Spaces - comprehensive LGBTQ2S+ professional development and training sessions for businesses and service providers (social services front-line staff municipalities etc.) offered as either single day workshops or multi day series to provide comprehensive diversity and inclusion training. Offered online and in-person. Strathcona County Pride - annual Pride Week created by the Pride Committee. Includes flag raising at County Hall with the Mayor and speeches youth events community events and educational opportunities. Often in collaboration with Strathcona County Family and Community Services Diversity & Inclusion NextGen Leadership Committee our organizational partners and the community at large. Peer Support Hours - flexible online and in-person peer support hours open to youth adults allies and families looking for guidance and resources. Online and in-person. Gemstones - in-person weekly community youth GSA in collaboration with Strathcona County Boys Girls Club at their youth hub The CanTEEN. Every Thursday evening offers a safe space for youth to make friends connections and having access to resources and information. Consistent and regular youth attending.

orgs.name: Edmonton Adaptive Sports Association
orgs.sub_category: Therapeutic programs for persons with disabilities
orgs.description: To educate and provide a positive experience for participants of all abilities through the sport of sledge hockey. Vision Statement: To encourage the physical well being and mental health of Participants. To provide education about the sport of sledge hockey to players coaches trainers managers referees and spectators. To promote positive shared experiences within the community. To fundraise and provide specialized equipment to enable people with a disability to be active within there community. To promote sledge hockey and increase participation. The Sledge Try It events are run by the Edmonton Adaptive Sports association (EASA) in order to provide individuals of all abilities with the opportunity to experience the sport of sledge hockey. The aim of the program includes aspects such as promoting physical activity building teamwork and promoting overall well being for participants. The participants have fun while learning the fundamentals of the sport (e.g. skating passing shooting) in a recreational environment. Members of EASA will be on hand to facilitate programming including coaches and/[layers. Our volunteers put in over 3000 hours to run our programs. We also offer TRY IT events to different organizations interested in giving sledge hockey a try. We provide sledges and sticks and have volunteers out on the ice for teaching the sport.

orgs.name: One in Christ Community Association of Alberta
orgs.description: During the summer we offered special programs for seniors and families ensuring that people of all ages can take part in something meaningful. These programs are designed to bring happiness encourage social interaction and strengthen community ties. Last year June 2023 the organization hosted a BBQ picnic which was a fun and lively event. Families friends and neighbors came together to enjoy delicious food games and music. It was a wonderful day filled with laughter and connection and many people appreciated the effort to create such a welcoming atmosphere. For children the organization partnered with a local church to organize a Community Kids Summer Camp. This camp provided children with a chance to play learn and make new friends in a safe and nurturing environment. Parents felt at ease knowing their kids were engaged in positive activities while building valuable life skills. In December One in Christ Community organized Community Christmas Program. This event was free of charge and welcomed about 250 people from the community. The program included festive decorations music and delicious food. Families came together to celebrate the season share stories and create cherished memories. It was a heartfelt event that highlighted the true meaning of Christmas—love joy and togetherness. In addition to these seasonal activities the organization holds monthly prayer meetings that are open to everyone. These gatherings take place in members’ homes or rented spaces to accommodate larger groups. The meetings provide a peaceful and supportive environment where people can come together to pray reflect and find encouragement. These gatherings play an important role in fostering a sense of faith-based community.

orgs.description: The Father’s House is dedicated to helping individuals find their way home to God and embrace a life of discipleship in Jesus Christ. We host a variety of Christian services and events designed for seniors families teens children and others. Our services held at two church locations welcome over 500 people weekly and offer music teaching and engaging activities for adults along with games lessons and crafts for children. Midweek programs for youth aged 12–18 feature worship teaching games and bus trips complementing our broader outreach that includes visitations to seniors shut-ins and hospital patients. In addition we operate a not-for-profit cafe—Higher Grounds—where individuals facing employment barriers volunteer to build their resumes while also providing meals for low-income individuals and families. Our church locations also have small groups—comprising five to forty members each—for Bible study and focused support groups (for men women parents mental health and more) thereby proving opportunities for deep friendships and spiritual growth. Furthermore our participation in community events such as parades festivals and block parties along with the organization of summer camps highlights our commitment to celebrating and strengthening the communities we serve.

orgs.name: Amy's House
orgs.description: IN MAY 2018 37-YEAR-OLD ... A MOTHER OF TWO AND DEVOTED WIFE TO ... WAS DIAGNOSED WITH STAGE 3B NON-SMALL CELL ADENOCARCINOMA LUNG CANCER. ... AN ULTRA-RUNNER TRIATHLETE AND FITNESS INSTRUCTOR WAS THE PICTURE OF HEALTH MAKING THE DIAGNOSIS A COMPLETE SHOCK TO HER FAMILY AND FRIENDS. DETERMINED TO RAISE AWARENESS ABOUT LUNG CANCER AND DISPEL THE MYTH THAT IT ONLY AFFECTS SMOKERS ... LAUNCHED THE LUNGES FOR LUNG CANCER CAMPAIGN. FOR EIGHT MONTHS SHE COMMITED TO DOING LUNGES DAILY EVEN FROM HER HOSPITAL ROOM SPREADING THE MESSAGE: 'IF YOU HAVE LUNGS YOU CAN GET LUNG CANCER.' ONE OF ... FINAL WISHES WAS TO CREATE A HOME WHERE CANCER PATIENTS ESPEICALLY THOSE FROM OUT OF TOWN COULD STAY WHILE UNDERGOING TREATMENT. SHE HAD OFTEN SPOKEN TO FELLOW PATIENTS WHO HAD TO ENDURE LONG EXHAUSTING DRIVES BACK AND FORTH FOR RADIATION OR CHEMOTHERAPY FURTHER TAXING THEIR HEALTH. ON SEPTEMBER 28 2019 ON WHAT WOULD HAVE BEEN ... 39TH BIRTHDAY AMY'S HOUSE 1 OFFICIALLY OPENED. THIS HOME PROVIDED A SANCTUARY FOR PATIENTS AND THEIR FAMILIES OFFERING A PLACE OF COMFORT DURING AN INCREDIBLY CHALLENGING TIME. IN MAY 2023 A SECOND HOME OPENED EXPANDING THE REACH OF HER DREAM. BOTH HOMES PROVIDE A COMFORTING ENVIRONMENT HELPING TO EASE THE EMOTIONAL AND PHYSICAL BURDENS OF CANCER TREATMENT. AMY'S HOUSE REPRESENTS THE FULFILLMENT OF HER DREAM-TO PROVIDE SUPPORT CONVENIENCE AND COMFORT FOR FAMILIES IN NEED JUST AS SHE AND HER OWN FAMILY WERE FORTUNATE ENOUGH TO RECEIVE DURING HER JOURNEY.

orgs.description: Community Options: A Society for Children and Families. Our organization strives to be a leader in the provision of inclusive quality programs and services for children and families. Our Community Preschool Education program provides inclusion opportunities throughout Edmonton region for children between 2.5 to 6 years of age. (Children must meet Alberta Education criteria for Program Unit Funding). Our staff of professionals develops an educational program individualized to meet childs additional needs. Parents are encouraged to be involved in family oriented programming and in decision making about the childs individual program plan. We operate Edmonton Northwest Child Care Centre Edmonton Northwest Out of School Care and Edmonton Northwest preschool program in the Inglewood neighborhood. We believe that children s programs should provide experiences that foster each child s growth and development as a total human being. This implies attention to the enhancement of skills in all areas of development social physical intellectual creative and emotional. Programs endeavor to create an environment where friendships are facilitated; each child learns positive concepts of him/her and others and establishes wholesome patterns for feeling and behaving. We also offer opportunities for families for social inclusion and support within this community through providing a number of community activities.

orgs.name: Autism Independent Living Association
orgs.sub_category: Services for adults and children with developmental disabilities
orgs.description: To relieve poverty by providing food and other basic necessities of life through subsidies to individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder who are in need. We are not currently providing food or other basic necessities at this time but plan to once we have our housing developed. Our housing development will be below market affordable housing and we may also be able to offer subsidies for autistic adults. We also hope to address food insecurity through gift certificates collective cooking and a collective food cooperative. We currently have a 12 unit apartment that we are looking at retrofitting for our first development and could potentially have that by the end of 2025. To relieve conditions associated with disability by providing specially adapted residential accommodation incidental facilities and support to individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder. Our housing will address the low income challenges that are common to autistic adults. We also reduce the social isolation that happens for autistic adults through our Health Wellness and Social Committee and Movie Club. The committee plans monthly social and learning activities that all of our members are welcome to attend. To advance education by providing life skills training to individuals who self-identify as having Autism Spectrum Disorder and the public. Supports provided through our 3 training programs: 1 for autistic board members 1 for general members and also our Resident Council Training program. Our board members are learning leadership skills business skills grant writing skills public speaking marketing and presentation skills. Our general members are learning healthy living skills independent living skills self awareness and self advocacy skills event planning fundraising and marketing skills. Our council members are learning conflict resolution skills effective communications skills problem solving skills tenancy rights and responsibilities and how to be an effective council and how to be responsive to landlord and other tenant needs. To undertake activities ancillary and incidental to the above charitable purposes. Our members are also learning social media and marketing skills presentation and public speaking skills organizational and time management skills through helping out on various initiatives and activities we have. We also work with other organizations that offer training and supports to autistic adults.

orgs.name: South Edmonton Fellowship Centre

orgs.description: 1) Telephone Addiction Support (780.220.7811) The Fellowship Centre phone number is available on the Fellowship Centre website in the Fellowship Newsletter and on the Canadian Mental Health Association (Edmonton) List of Resources for People with Addictions. Volunteers answer the phone from 9:00 AM to 9:00 PM 365 days a year providing addiction peer-support as well as information about the Centre and about available support for addiction recovery. 2) Fellowship Newsletter (https://fellowship-centre.org) The Fellowship Newsletter is available by online subscription; paper copies are available at the Centre. Past newsletters are accessible on the Fellowship Centre’s website. The newsletter includes recovery information and a calendar of monthly recovery support meetings and events held at the Centre. 3) Twelve Step Addiction Recovery Meetings There are currently 26 weekly 12-Step mutual support recovery meetings held at the Fellowship Centre including Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) Cocaine Anonymous (CA) Gamblers Anonymous (GA) Sex Addicts Anonymous (SAA) and Overeaters Anonymous (OA). 4) Fellowship Library The Fellowship Library lends books magazines and audio-visual material relevant to understanding and recovering from addiction. To ensure anonymity library material is not signed out. Those who visit the Centre take library material that they feel may help them and return it when they are finished. 5) Social Events Social isolation characterizes individuals as their addiction progresses. Coming out of isolation and regaining a sense of community is essential to the recovery process. Supportive human connection is considered a type of addiction treatment for sustaining long-term recovery. The Fellowship Centre has had many social events since it opened in 2021 with more being planned. 6) Volunteer Opportunities and Support Volunteering is generally associated with improved quality of life. It is an essential aspect of both 12-Step and SMART addiction recovery programs. Operation and maintenance of the Fellowship Centre and its programs are entirely dependent upon substantial and continuous volunteer efforts. Such efforts help many maintain recovery from addiction.

orgs.name: Hope and Care Canada Association
orgs.description: Hope and Care Canada Association is a not-for-profit and registered charitable organization governed by a passionate and dedicated volunteer Board of Directors. The association is founded to help new refugees and immigrants integrate into the Canadian society successfully. Hope and Care's Tutoring Program provides children and youth tutoring services for academic success in preparation for a pathway to access and succeed in post-secondary education. Hope and Care conducts regular mentoring sessions for the youth. Becoming a mentor helps a young person do better in school understand their strengths and reach their goals. One of the aims of our mentoring program is to help prevent the youth from dropping out of school involvement in drugs and gangs and prepare them for better choices that will make them succeed in society. Hope and Care Canada Association sponsors refugees because as a community we felt obligations to respond to refugee needs. All most all the members and volunteers of this organization are former refugee who understands what it means to be a refugee and the pain they go through by fleeing their countries to save their lives. The settlement support services Hope and Care offer to refugees and new immigrants include: finding housing providing household items clothing and other basic necessities orienting newly arrived refugees to the transportation systems connecting them with community services offering friendship moral and emotional support.

The transition from the Pandemic and the ongoing societal struggles has created stress and isolation for most families and persons with developmental disabilities. In order to reach out to families and individuals we offered workshops opportunities to share through coffee meetings additional information through our website and reach out by meeting with families in person as well as through zoom phone and social media. Over 1 200 hours was spent talking to supporting and preparing families and individuals with developmental disabilities.

orgs.description: The Fort Saskatchewan Public Library is committed to enriching the lives of area residents through the provision of diverse resources and engaging programs. Furthermore we facilitate access to a wide range of digital resources such as online databases eBooks and eAudiobooks. Recognizing the diverse needs of our community the library offers complimentary programs for patrons of all ages and extends its services through a dedicated delivery program for reading materials to local seniors' lodges. Public access to computers and wireless internet is also provided free of charge. Our innovative Collaboratory provides a dynamic environment equipped with resources such as gaming consoles and a green screen. We provide access to a sewing machine a die-cut machine photo conversion station and button makers supporting creative exploration and skill development. In support of lifelong learning and career advancement the library maintains a dedicated career station offering resources for job interviews and training including appointments to a resume tutor. The Fort Saskatchewan Public Library remains a vital community hub dedicated to fostering literacy learning and connection.

orgs.name: ONE STEP LEARNING OPPORTUNITIES CENTRE
orgs.description: Our Story Literacy and brain development are crucial globally starting from early childhood. Over 40 years ago the founders of One Step Learning began advocating for early childhood literacy in Calgary and Edmonton after immigrating from Ghana. With support from a Canadian couple they enrolled their children in licensed daycare despite high costs and minimal subsidies. They saw the benefits of early literacy when their children quickly developed. They promoted these ideas especially within African immigrant communities who often kept children at home due to daycare expenses. Government subsidies now reduce daycare costs lessening the need for such advocacy in Canada. In 2019 after visiting their hometown of Entumbil Ghana the founders assessed the community's needs with town representatives and donated part of their property to create an early childhood education facility for 30 years rent-free. One Step Learning Opportunities Centre (OSL) was incorporated in Alberta Canada to connect with supporters of early childhood learning. OSL obtained charitable status from the Canada Revenue Agency in August 2020 enabling it to issue tax credit receipts for donations. A daycare for children aged 0-6 started in Entumbil in October 2021. Support from various collaborators for the daycare has greatly impacted the community especially children girls and women. OSL appreciates this support and seeks additional collaborators for sustainability over the next two years. For more details see our 2024 Financial Statements and 2025-2029 Strategic Business Plan. Learn more: www.onesteplearning.org Mission Provide affordable early childhood education to rural Entumbil Ghana community and towns by partnering with Canadians and others who support childhood charitable causes. Vision To prepare children ages 0-6 to be proficient bilinguals in both English and the local language using STEAM concepts and ensure their readiness for elementary school. Impact Literacy development on-going for over 80 rural children daily across 5 towns daily Empowerment of girls and women allowing parents to work Secure safe and healthy Centre established for children's well-being Started with 11 now serve 80 children daily (exceeding the planned 32) Creation of 14 jobs (8 academic 6 support staff) Addressing sustainable development goals (SDG 4) Tax receipt opportunities for donors Value Proposition is that it cost less than $70 per month per child for literacy & wellbeing

orgs.legal_name: CAMEROONIAN ASSOCIATION OF EDMONTON/ASSOCIATION CAMEROUNAISED'EDMONTON (CAE-ACE)
orgs.description: The Cameroonian Association of Edmonton (CAE-ACE) offers a wide range of community-focused programs designed to support integration cultural preservation empowerment and well-being for Cameroonians and the wider African diaspora in Edmonton. 1. Welcome & Integration Network (WIN): Helps newcomers adapt to life in Edmonton by offering support resources and community connections that ease their settlement and integration journey. 2. IWDIMAA Youth Program: Equips Cameroonian youth with mentorship leadership development and cultural education. This program fosters confidence resilience and a strong sense of identity among young community members. 3. Cameroonian Women’s Club: A vibrant and supportive space where women come together to share experiences build relationships and participate in initiatives that empower and uplift them. 4. ACE Tax Clinic: Provides free and confidential tax filing services for low-income individuals and families ensuring they access eligible benefits and remain in good financial standing. 5. Heritage Program: Celebrates and promotes Cameroonian culture through events storytelling food language dance and historical education—keeping traditions alive and fostering pride in cultural roots. 6. Musango Voice: A community choir that brings together individuals of all ages to express their cultural heritage through music. The group performs at events creating unity and joy through song. 7. ACE Digitizing Program (ADP): A digital literacy initiative that offers training and access to technology for individuals who wish to improve their computer and internet skills for education work or daily life. 8. Sports & Wellbeing Program (SWP): Encourages physical activity and mental health through recreational sports fitness sessions and wellness workshops for both youth and adults. 9. ACE Resilience Program (ARP): Strengthens personal and community resilience by providing access to mental health resources peer support networks and tools to navigate life’s challenges. Together these programs reflect CAE-ACE’s ongoing commitment to building a strong inclusive and culturally vibrant Cameroonian community in Edmonton.

orgs.name: Thou Art Here Theatre Guild
orgs.sub_category: Theatre / performing arts (drama / comedy / musical / puppetry / etc.)
orgs.description: Purpose - To advance the public’s appreciation of the arts by producing public art exhibitions presentations and performance art(s) events and by providing a forum forqualifi ed artists to exhibit present or perform their artistic works through participation in such events. Self Produced Performances: For each self produced performance we hire a dynamic team of qualified professional artists (including actors designers directors and technicans) who work together to create and perform/exhibit their artistic work. Ongoing self produced performances include: A. 'Civil Blood: A Treaty Story' a new Canadian play by Josh Languedoc & Neil Bye-Kuefler that explores the complex tensions between First Nations and the European Settlers at the end of the fur trade. Languedoc weaves the texts of 'Romeo and Juliet' Treaty #6 and his own learnings of traditional stories into a reimagined contemporary tale. The play will be staged as an immersive split narrative experience in the historically authentic 1876 Amiskwaciwâskahikan fort (?????????????? ) culminating in a community gathering and artist exchange led by First Nations Elders and knowledge keepers. B. 'Cycle' by Andrew Ritchie a solo-show told from a stationary bike this in-development performance explores Ritchie’s personal experience history and politics of active transportation and cycle culture in Canada. Lucky audience members seated on stationary bikes will be asked to pedal alongside Ritchie as he traverses the dangers and highs of urban transportation and gig work culture. Inspired by true experiences as a bike food courier in Toronto and the financial and physical precariousness of trying to ‘make a living’ in Canada.

orgs.description: Children - We are passionate about discipling our children and teenagers to become faithful followers of Jesus Christ by teaching the whole counsel of God from the Holy Bible which is God’s word to man as our final authority. orgs.name: GOODWILL INDUSTRIES OF ALBERTA (REGISTERED SOCIETY)
orgs.description: Goodwill Industries of Alberta (Registered Society) is a social enterprise providing individuals with disabilities the opportunity to enhance their lives through meaningful employment. Direct charitable programs include Career Connections (Path to Employment) program which is a multi-service program for individuals with disabilities as well as the operation of donation collection and thrift store operation where skills and experiences are provided to persons with disabilities. Goodwill provides industry specific skills training career counselling and employment preparation and job research to obtain paid employment or volunteer work supporting the need of both clients and employers. You Can Ride (YCR2) is a program that supports the belief that every child should experience the joy and freedom of riding a bike. The program fits modifies and lend adaptive bikes to children with disabilities to help them overcome barriers and lead to productive and healthy lives. Goodwill@Work aims to create micro-social enterprises providing persons with disabilities the opportunity for new and enhanced work experience including the potential to own and operate their own businesses and which provide complementary services to other activities at Goodwill. Goodwill also delivers programming to help support multi-barriered Albertans increase their labour market participation and gain independence by assisting them to prepare for obtain and maintain employment.

IN ADDITION WE OFFER GRIEF SUPPORT PROGRAMS FOR CHILDREN TEENS ADULTS AND FAMILIES GRIEVING THE LOSS OF A LOVED ONE. THE ADULT DAY PROGRAM A WELLNESS PROGRAM FOR PEOPLE WHO ARE STILL LIVING IN THE COMMUNITY AND REQUIRE SERVICES TO HELP MAINTAIN OR IMPROVE THEIR PHYSICAL AND COGNITIVE FUNCTION (INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO THOSE WITH A PROGRESSIVE LIFE-THREATENING OR LIFE-LIMITING ILLNESS).

orgs.description: During 2024 the CHILD Foundation continued its ongoing programs of poverty relief disaster relief and education in Haiti India and South Africa. For poverty relief CHILD sent $36 000 to the Haitian Children's Aid Society (Canadian charity) to support a program which feeds over 300 malnourished children in Haiti as well as for medications and staff scholarships. In India CHILD provided $18 406 for rice and protein-rich foods for 120 children in a children's home run by Metropolitan Mission (MM) in M.V. Gudem in addition to $5 000 for Christmas clothes and blankets for widows around Vijayawada Andhra Pradesh and $10 000 for a tailoring program. $18 041 was also sent to Metropolitan Mission to provide milk eggs and fruit to children living in poverty in a school in Hyderabad. For disaster relief in India CHILD sent $10 000 for the drilling of wells in the drought-stricken state of Andhra Pradesh as well as $7 000 for food and essential supplies for victims of flood and displacement. For the education of young students CHILD provided $34 608 for teachers' salaries and bonuses and $10 467 for books and uniforms for the students at the Creo Harvey Primary and Alpha Creo schools run by MM in India. CHILD also continued supporting 'Smoking & Alcohol Harms Alleviation & Rehabilitation Association' (SAHARA) in South Africa with $44 000 which was used for staff salaries and purchasing medications to help people overcome substance use disorder. SAHARA assists people to reduce or stop alcohol tobacco or drug use thereby limiting harm within the community. SAHARA provides treatment and medicines free of charge to people and provides training for service providers in management of substance use disorder.

orgs.name: JOHN HUMPHREY CENTRE FOR PEACE AND HUMAN RIGHTS
orgs.description: Engage children and young people in peace-building and human rights education. Foster adult learning and build community collaboration through education and dialogue on peace and human rights. Work with government businesses and organizations to strengthen their application of a human rights lens. Stride Advocacy - Since 2017 Stride Advocacy has supported community human rights issues. JHC has been a place of last resort for many over the years and Stride evolved as an effort to ensure we don’t just 'refer' people and ensure they are connected to what they need to move forward. The John Humphrey Centre for Peace and Human Rights (JHC) is proud to work in partnership with Righting Relations Canada a heart-led pan-Canadian network of adult educators and community organizers working for social change. Human Rights Commission Research - Thanks to the support of Gurcharan Bhatia JHC initiated a research project examining the human rights mechanism at the federal level by the Canadian Human Rights Commission and the Canadian Human Rights Tribunal. The project identified barriers experienced by complainants and how the Commission needs to be strengthened to be accessible to marginalized community members. JHC wants to contribute to improving GBV services for at-risk groups by using an intersectional lens to understand and collect community-based best practices for delivering GBV services and support. We will also combine the experiences of clients workers and sector leaders to collectively think and implement. Edmonton Activism Project Inspiring Change: Learning Activism from Older Generations In 2024 the John Humphrey Centre for Peace and Human Rights launched an impactful initiative documenting the life’s work of 22 senior activists who championed human rights in Edmonton since the 1960s. This project spotlighted diverse forms of activism addressing topics like immigrant women’s rights racism and discrimination queer rights Indigenous knowledge in addressing injustice houselessness disability rights peace education and anti-war efforts. Rural Youth Anti-Racism Celebrating Educating & Acting on Rights The John Humphrey Centre for Peace and Human Rights (JHC) achieved significant milestones through its 2024-2025 Youth-Led Rural Anti-Racism Initiative aimed at equipping young leaders with the knowledge tools and opportunities to address systemic racism and build more inclusive rural communities. Centered on youth empowerment.

orgs.name: SpeechDojo Education Foundation
orgs.description: SpeechDojo’s mission is to equip students with the public speaking skills they need to succeed in their academics careers and societies. SpeechDojo seeks to bridge this educational void through our two public speaking programs delivered within schools – Classroom and Online. The Classroom program involves weekly 45-minute instruction over Google Meet for a total of 15 weeks. It is geared towards students in grades 4-9 with a different bite size topic like 'volume pitch and pacing' or 'writing a speech' covered each week. The focus of this program is confidence-building and half the time is spent on an interactive activity. The Online program has a hybrid delivery model: students in grades 9-12 participate in an introductory and wrap-up 'Dojo drop-in' workshop with the core of the program being our asynchronous gamified online courses. Our three courses - 'Fundamentals of Public Speaking' 'Becoming Presentation Savvy' and 'Acing the Job Search' - were developed filmed and embedded into a gamified learning platform ourselves. Students work through the course during their leadership or career and life skills classes. To-date we have taught or are currently teaching 101 classes and 2620 students in the Classroom program and 12 classes and 300 students through the Online program which was launched last year. In addition to making public speaking education accessible through our in-school programming we also share communication and career development tips on our social media which have over 31 000 followers. Our team consists of 54 dedicated undergraduate and high school volunteers in Edmonton Toronto and Vancouver across our four teams: Classroom Online Marketing and Finance. By focusing on confidence-building and integration with the school curriculum SpeechDojo is committed to building vital communication skills in students. Our goal is to empower students to advocate for themselves in the classroom and ultimately the workforce and broader society.

orgs.description: Forward In Faith Christian Ministries International (Alberta) continued to advance its charitable mission throughout 2024 by delivering a wide range of faith-based and community-oriented programs. These ongoing programs were led by volunteers ministry leaders and church members and directly supported the organization’s objectives of spiritual growth community engagement and holistic development. Children’s Ministry: Weekly Sunday school classes provided biblical education to children aged 3–14 using interactive materials and age-appropriate teaching methods. Seasonal events such as Christmas and Easter plays helped children understand Christian values in engaging and creative ways. Attendance ranged from 15 to 25 children weekly supported by five volunteer teachers. Youth Ministry: Weekly Friday evening Bible study and fellowship sessions focused on discipleship character development and leadership skills for youth aged 15–25. Organized quarterly outreach and recreational events (e.g. sports day movie nights) to build relationships and foster a sense of belonging. Youth were encouraged to volunteer within other ministries to build responsibility and spiritual maturity. Women’s Ministry: Bi-weekly prayer meetings and monthly Bible study sessions focused on women’s spiritual development mental health and family leadership roles. Special events included Mother’s Day celebrations wellness workshops and empowerment seminars. Men’s Ministry: Monthly men’s fellowship breakfasts and discipleship programs addressed topics such as spiritual leadership fatherhood and financial stewardship. Community service projects encouraged men to give back through volunteer maintenance work and outreach to families in need. Family Support Services: Offered marital counseling pre-marital guidance and parenting support through one-on-one sessions and group workshops. Supported over 10 families during times of crisis through spiritual counseling meals and prayer. Weekly Worship Services and Prayer Meetings: Conducted regular Sunday worship services Wednesday Bible study and Friday night prayer meetings attended by members of all ages. These services were foundational to the church’s mission.

orgs.name: Edmonton Heritage Council Society
orgs.description: We connect people to the stories of our city by helping Edmontonians research preserve interpret and advocate for our heritage. The Edmonton Heritage Council has undertaken a number of initiatives that explore Edmonton’s past and present and look toward the city’s future with the goal of providing Edmontonians a deeper understanding of who they are. The FIRE Grant program (Funding Indigenous Resurgence in Edmonton) provides funding assistance—up to $10 000—to Indigenous (First Nations Metis and Inuit) individuals and organizations to support projects that help tell important stories about our community. The FIRE grant program is designed by Indigenous people for Indigenous people. This program supports Indigenous peoples’ inherent right to self-determination and cultural resurgence and we hope to provide folks with the support and resources to advance their brilliant work. The Edmonton City As Museum Project tells the best stories Edmonton has to offer from the perspective of Edmontonians. A stepping stone to an eventual bricks and mortar city museum the Edmonton City As Museum Project uses the web to preserve and present Edmonton’s urban heritage: the people places things and moments that make us who we are. Far from a dusty archive the Edmonton City As Museum Project—or #ECAMP—offers a colourful look at this multifaceted city. The Edmonton Heritage Network facilitates connections between Edmonton’s heritage stakeholders. It aims to break down silos build relationships between heritage organizations and facilitate projects that respond to shared needs.Edmonton’s heritage organizations tell the story of the city from different perspectives. The Edmonton Heritage Network aims to unify these narratives to join perspectives that may seem disparate but together make up the fabric of our urban history. Edmonton Maps Heritage is a collective active and ongoing 'mapping' of the city’s heritage. It anticipates broader public involvement in continually adding more content on Edmonton's experience and culture historically culturally and artistically. We hope that users will connect with the site visually and functionally but above all find that the content enriches their sense of their city and community.

orgs.name: Princen Sammy Eduful & Herty Foundation
orgs.sub_category: Foundations funding community benefit QDs in general
orgs.description: Princen Sammy Eduful & Herty foundation is a duly registered social and human services charitable organization headquartered in Edmonton. Serving the communities of Edmonton NW Calgary Airdrie Lethbridge St.Albert the city of Fort Saskatchewan AJAX Pickering Whitby North York GTA London Ontario Montreal QC and operating satellite station facilities located across Canada. As a tax exempt non profit organization dedicated to youth empowerment leadership development and workforce readiness we bridge gaps for underrepresented communities. This vital initiative aligns with ESDC and our shared commitment to empowering minorities particularly Black Indigenous and other racialized youth. Through internship and job readiness programs which are designed to provide students with opportunities to gain work work experience develop skills as they prepare to enter an ever-changing workforce. Youth empowerment and internship job readiness programs during the summer which provide students/trainees with the opportunity to gain knowledge develop skills and work habits that increase the potential for future employment success. Princen Foundation currently providing support services financial aid gift cards for groceries and food aid to approximately 75 000 families. Many low families were hit hardest by the current cost of living and high food prices as savings and income dwindled. By providing immediate financial support for hunger relief food security and to purchase food gift cards for groceries and other essential supplies for minorities and low income families because of lack of access and also experiencing interrupted support services in the community. Helping to provide resources to purchase food gift cards for groceries clothing and footwear to deliver other essential supplies for children & families especially vulnerable seniors to ensure the continuity of essential services for the at risk children families and seniors and those most affected by the current situation. When women are empowered it allows them to have more control over their own career. In response to the COVID19 pandemic Princen Sammy Foundation has provided an emergency small relief fund of $250 for an average family of five for more than 50 000 children families & seniors to deliver nutritious food and empower families to make healthier choices.

orgs.description: MEIKA'S SAFEHOUSE IS A REGISTERED CHARITABLE ORGANIZATION WHO'S PURPOSE IS TO REHABILITATE AND PROVIDE A SAFE AND LOVING ENVIRONMENT FOR ANY BIRD IN NEED. WE WORK PRIMARILY WITH PARROTS BUT ALL SPECIES OF COMPANION OR PET BIRDS ARE WELCOMED. WHEN BIRDS ARE SURRENDERED INTO OUR CARE WE FULLY ASSESS THEIR OVERALL HEALTH AND START SOME TRAINING AND SOCIALIZATION AS APPROPRIATE. MOST OF THE BIRDS THAT COME INTO CARE HAVE NOT BEEN ABUSED BUT BECAUSE OF THE LEVEL OF INTELLIGENCE THEY POSSES THE Y ARE OFTEN UNDER SIGNIFICANT EMOTIONAL STRESS WHEN THEY ARE RELINQUISHED. BIRDS THAT HAVE BEEN MISTREATED EMOTIONALLY OR PHYSICALLY REQUIRE MORE REHABILITATION AND MAY NEVER BE SUITABLE FOR REHOMING. WHEN WE DETERMINE A BIRD IS READY TO BE REHOMED MUCH CARE AND CONSIDERATION IS PUT INTO SELECTING AN APPROPRIATE FAMILY. WHEN WE ARE ABLE TO MATCH A BIRD A NEW FAMILY IN MOST CASES HE OR SHE WILL BE ADOPTED WITH A SUITABLE CAGE AS WELL AS THEIR TOYS AND FAVORITE ITEMS THAT THEY HAVE GROWN ACCUSTOMED TO. WE ALSO PROVIDE A CURRENT HEALTH CERTIFICATE AND MICROCHIP ALL SMALL TO EXTRA LARGE BIRDS BEFORE THEY LEAVE OUR CARE.

orgs.name: Canadian Grand Masters Fiddling Association
orgs.legal_name: CANADIAN GRAND MASTERS FIDDLING CHAMPIONSHIP
orgs.description: In keeping with the association's mandate of preserving and promoting Canadian fiddling the main program that the Canadian Grand Masters Fiddling Association (CGMFA) holds is the annual national fiddling competition. After a very successful event in Winnipeg Manitoba in 2022 and the competition held in Truro Nova Scotia in August 2023 the national championship was held in Yukon for the first time in the territories. It was a great success with approximately 30 competitors and upwards of 400 people that attended the weekend festivities. It was an exciting event that brought together various regional styles of Canadian fiddling and also served as an opportunity to showcase the significant contributions of Canadian and a youth summit for educational purposes. We continue offering an online fiddle workshop series to keep active and present throughout the year. In an effort to promote regional styles and ensure that there remains a teaching & learning component to the Board's work this has been a successful pursuit. These workshops started in September 2022 and were every month or so and are ongoing.

orgs.description: RONALD MCDONALD HOUSE CHARITIES ALBERTA SUPPORTS FAMILIES SEEKING VITAL MEDICAL TREATMENT FOR THEIR SERIOUSLY ILL OR INJURED CHILD. OUR WARM COMPASSIONATE HOUSE PROVIDE A HOME-AWAY-FROM-HOME FOR FAMILIES WHO NEED TO TRAVEL FOR MEDICAL REASONS. WHEN THOSE FAMILIES ARE EXPERIENCING ONE OF THE MOST DIFFICULT TIMES OF THEIR LIVES – WE OFFER THEM COMFORT IN BEING ABLE TO STAY TOGETHER. SINCE THE FIRST HOUSES WERE BUILT IN ALBERTA IN 1985 WE HAVE SUPPORTED TENS OF THOUSANDS OF FAMILIES. EVERY YEAR THOUSANDS WILL STAY AT ONE OF ALBERTA’S RONALD MCDONALD HOUSES. THESE STAYS CAN BE A COUPLE OF NIGHTS OR CAN LAST FOR WEEKS OR MONTHS AT A TIME. EACH RONALD MCDONALD HOUSE HAS FAMILY SUITES FOR FAMILIES TO REST. THE HOUSES HAVE OPEN KITCHENS WHERE A FAMILY CAN SIT DOWN AND SHARE A HOMEMADE MEAL TOGETHER ALONGSIDE OTHER FAMILIES GOING THROUGH SIMILAR EXPERIENCES. THE SENSE OF COMMUNITY ENABLES FAMILIES TO RELY ON ONE ANOTHER WHEN THEY NEED IT MOST. A RONALD MCDONALD HOUSE SAVES FAMILIES HUNDREDS TO THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS ON ACCOMMODATION TRANSPORTATION MEALS LAUNDRY AND MUCH MORE EACH YEAR. HAVING A RONALD MCDONALD HOUSE CLOSE TO THE HOSPITAL IS AN IMPORTANT ELEMENT OF FAMILY-CENTERED CARE. RONALD MCDONALD HOUSE CHARITIES ALBERTA RELIES ON THE SUPPORT OF VOLUNTEERS TO HELP EXECUTE PROGRAMMING SERVICES AND EVENTS FOR MORE INFORMATION PLEASE VISIT WWW.RMHCALBERTA.ORG

orgs.description: Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Edmonton: Overview of Ministries and Services The Ethiopian Evangelical Church of Edmonton operates through two distinct branches each serving the unique needs of its congregation. 1. It offers a range of programs and services designed to nurture spiritual growth provide support and strengthen community ties. - Sunday Worship: Weekly worship services focused on teaching the gospel of Jesus Christ and fostering fellowship with God. - Mid-Week Outreach: Various outreach programs held during the week to engage members and the broader community in spiritual development and service. - Support Services: Assistance provided to both members and non-members to help them live according to Evangelical Christian principles. - Counseling Services: Support is offered by church leaders volunteer counseling ministries and deacons to address social emotional financial and mental health challenges. The church provides intervention strategies and practical solutions as part of its pastoral care. - Youth and Children’s Ministry: Programs and outreach events designed for children of Ethiopian and Eritrean expatriates facilitated by both adult and youth volunteers. - Missionary Activities: Partnerships with other churches and ministries to provide care support and accommodation for children in rural areas of Ethiopia. - Partnerships and Sponsorships: The church collaborates with various organizations and charitable entities to: - Sponsor children in Ethiopia; - Support Ethiopian and Eritrean refugees in different in and out side of Canada; - Provide financial aid to churches and individuals in Africa and the Middle East. - Refugee Support in Canada: The church plays an active role in refugee sponsorship working in collaboration with its members and the Government of Canada under official sponsorship agreements to facilitate the resettlement of refugees. 2. Hybrid Church The second and growing branch is the Hybrid Church which primarily consists of second-generation Canadians. orgs.description: AUTISM SERVICE DOGS: HAVE A VEST AND HAVE PUBLIC ACCESS WITH THEIR CLIENT FOR OUR PROGRAM THE CHILD MUST HAVE A DIAGNOSIS OF AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER. PARENTS WHO HAVE AN AUTISTIC CHILD CAN APPLY FROM WHEN THEY ARE 3 TO 10 YEARS OLD. WE WILL ONLY PROVIDE A DOG TO THEM WHEN THE CHILD IS BETWEEN THE AGES OF 5 AND 13 YEARS OLD. THE PURPOSE OF TEH DOG IS TO PROVIDE GROUNDING AND SUPPORT WHEN A CHILD IS BECOMING DYSREGULATED OR IS HAVING A MELTDOWN. THEY CAN ACT AS A CALMING COMPANION TO THE CHILD AND ALSO AID IN PEER FACILITIATION. MOBILITY SERVICE DOGS: HAVE A VEST AND HAVE PUBLIC ACCESS WITH THEIR CLIENT MAIN TASKS INCLUDE: RETRIEVAL (TO GET BRING IT GIVE) OPENING DOORS/CUPBOARDS (TUG) CLOSING DOORS/DRAWERS (PUSH) TURNING ON/OFF LIGHTS (LIGHT) SUPPORTING AN INDIVIDUAL MOVING FROM ONE AREA TO ANOTHER. OUR DOGS HELP SOMEONE WITH A PHYSICAL DISABILITY IN THIS CASE. FACILITY DOGS: HAVE A VET BUT DO NOT HAVE PUBLIC ACCESS WITH THEIR CLIENT THE PURPOSE OF THE DOG IS TO PROVIDE GROUNDING AND SUPPORT WHEN SOMEONE IS BECOMING DYSREGULATED OR THEIR SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM IS FIRING (FIGHT OR FLIGHT). THIS IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR INDIVIDUALS WHO HAVE EXPERIENCED TRAUMA. COMPANION DOGS: DO NOT HAVE A VEST AND DO NOT HAVE PUBLIC ACCESS WITH THEIR CLIENT COMPANION DOGS ARE FOR CLIENTS THAT NEED EXTRA SUPPORT IN THE HOME FOR A VARIETY OF REASONS (CLIENT DEPENDENT) BUT THEY DO NOT NEED THE EXTRA SUPPORT IN PUBLIC.

orgs.name: Thousand Faces Festival Association
orgs.description: The program provided by the society is its namesake: the Thousand Faces festival. In late June of every year we bring multicultural multidisciplinary artists together with culturally and economically diverse audiences for a festival of performance and participatory workshops that bring the public together to explore and enjoy the mythic stories and art forms at the foundations of the world’s diverse cultures. The festival has developed long-term relationships with several accomplished artists from under represented communities who taken together make up an ecosystem of art and myth. The festival puts a premium on accessibility and no one is refused to entry to an event because they cannot pay. The dance Theatre Music and spoken word offered at the festival often evolves into significant artistic expressions shared beyond the festival.

orgs.name: Al-Jawad Islamic Foundation of Edmonton
orgs.description: The Al-Jawad Islamic Foundation of Edmonton is a nonprofit organization that serves the local Shia Muslim community. Its main purpose is to hold events and programs about the Shia religion and to share the teachings of the Ahlulbayt (peace be upon them). The foundation organizes gatherings lectures and commemorations during important times in the Islamic calendar. These events help community members come together learn about their faith and remember important figures and lessons from Shia history. Al-Jawad also works to support families and youth making sure the next generation stays connected to their faith and traditions. In short the foundation’s goal is to bring people together strengthen their faith and build a supportive community in Edmonton
